headline: High-risk filesystem and shell execution in AutoGen can collide with a non-runnable, network-disabled second profile; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are limited by the second profile’s lack of runtime surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read files, run subprocesses, and use stdin/stdout, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content if the operator bridges outputs manually. The second profile has no runtime surfaces or runnable agent behavior, so there is no documented automatic channel from awesome-python back into AutoGen. This makes the pathway possible but narrow.
conditions: IF the operator copies awesome-python content into AutoGen prompts or files
IF AutoGen is configured to treat file contents as instructions
mitigations: Keep the two agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted content into AutoGen prompts
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from imported text
Review any file-fed content before AutoGen reads it

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen can read and write its working directory and send model-provider API traffic, while awesome-python is a non-runnable repository with no declared data-handling surface. A leakage path exists only if sensitive application data is placed into AutoGen’s workspace and then manually transferred elsewhere; the second profile itself does not expose a documented exfiltration channel.
conditions: IF sensitive application data is stored in AutoGen’s configured working directory
IF that data is manually copied into artifacts associated with awesome-python
mitigations: Store sensitive files outside AutoGen’s workspace
Use separate OS users for the two profiles
Redact secrets before any manual transfer
Audit the working directory before and after runs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has broad shell, filesystem, and subprocess capabilities, but awesome-python is not runnable and declares no write or network capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable resource shown in the profiles, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced. Uncertainty is resolved upward only if the operator adds a shared writable directory.
conditions: IF both profiles are pointed at the same writable directory
IF the operator turns awesome-python into an executable workflow
mitigations: Do not mount a shared writable directory
Run AutoGen in a container with isolated storage
Keep awesome-python as read-only reference material
Avoid concurrent edits to the same git checkout

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate outputs from code-executing agents, but awesome-python is only a static collection and cannot verify or act on those outputs. The pair therefore lacks a documented default chain where B treats A as authoritative; any cascade would require the operator to repurpose the repository into an execution step.
conditions: IF outputs from AutoGen are copied into a downstream automation built from awesome-python
IF the operator disables human review of AutoGen outputs
mitigations: Require human review before acting on AutoGen outputs
Log provenance for any copied outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles. AutoGen touches application data and model-provider keys, while awesome-python is a static repository with no declared data classes or residency/retention obligations. Because the second profile has no operational data flow, there is no documented residency or retention breach to cite.
conditions: IF the operator introduces regulated data into AutoGen’s workspace
IF a separate deployment policy is attached to awesome-python
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document any residency requirements before deployment
Use a separate compliant system for regulated workloads
